Executive Summary This project, Production of Pipeline Grade Renewable Natural Gas and Value-Added Chemicals from Forest Biomass Residues, was commissioned to advance the state of cellulosic biomass to renewable gas (RG) technologies by leveraging an existing pilot-scale gasification system and an existing catalytic reactor with downstream separation processes to upgrade forest biomass- derived syngas to methane-rich RG and mixed-alcohol byproducts. The final RG product requirements include meeting heat content standards of 990-1150 BTU/scf and total sulfur of less than 12.6 parts per million by volume (ppmv) with >2.5 scfm of RG output. Herein a techno-economic analysis was performed around the West Biofuels mixed alcohol process leveraging, where appropriate, inputs from previous reports on biomass gasification (e.g., NREL: Dutta, 2011 [1], West Biofuels ARV-15-017 [2]). The studied reactor and catalyst system can be operated in such a manner as to prioritize either the production of alcohols or RG and consequently two scenarios were selected for analysis to examine the limits of performance. The calculated production cost and quality of the renewable gas and ethanol products in each respective case is provided in Tables EX1 – EX2. These data show that in the absence of CO 2 credits (i.e., from carbon sequestration, 45Q), the estimated costs to reach pipeline/distribution quality products are $22.60/MMBtu for renewable gas in the high RG scenario and $3.83/gal EtOH in the high alcohol synthesis scenario.
